item.text: {"search_note":"I found several strong institutional-design signals, but very little direct 2024 evidence that those institutions had already become self-sustaining, independent of Tinubu’s personal control. Most positive items are initiation or staffing; most negative items are about weak oversight, patronage risk, or repression.","evidence":[{"title":"President Tinubu Establishes Comprehensive Economic Coordination and Planning System for Nigeria","publisher":"State House","date":"2024-03-27","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-comprehensive-economic-coordination-and-planning-system-for-nigeria/","summary":"Tinubu created PECC and EET structures centered on the finance minister and CBN governor, with economists and private-sector figures, and ordered rapid implementation of the emergency plan. This is strong evidence of institutionalized, technocratic coordination that could outlive the presidency.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.7"]},{"title":"In Detail: The Student Loan (Access to Higher Education) Act, 2024","publisher":"State House","date":"2024-04-04","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/in-detail-the-student-loan-access-to-higher-education-act-2024/","summary":"The student-loan law broadened access to higher education and skills training and created a standing fund and delivery structure. This is one of the clearest examples of a potentially durable social institution rather than a one-off payout.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8"]},{"title":"President Tinubu Appoints Management Team of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund","publisher":"State House","date":"2024-04-05","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-appoints-management-team-of-the-nigerian-education-loan-fund/","summary":"Tinubu appointed a management team described as qualified professionals to stand up NELFUND. That supports a merit-based institutional build, though it remains an early-stage staffing signal rather than proof of durable performance.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8"]},{"title":"President Tinubu Directs Reorganisation of the Bureau of Public Procurement","publisher":"State House","date":"2024-06-15","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-reorganisation-of-the-bureau-of-public-procurement/","summary":"Procurement reform is a concrete effort to improve transparency and value for money in a core state institution. If sustained, this is the kind of administrative reform that can outlast a single leader.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.7"]},{"title":"My Resolve To Enhance Nigeria’s Security Unwavering – President Tinubu","publisher":"State House","date":"2024-04-22","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/my-resolve-to-enhance-nigerias-security-unwavering-president-tinubu/","summary":"Tinubu framed state policing as a way to improve accountability, safeguard civil liberties, and fit policing to community needs. This is a positive institutional signal, but still mostly policy rhetoric.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","4B.4"]},{"title":"President Tinubu Launches National Resettlement Scheme for Conflict Victims","publisher":"State House","date":"2024-07-06","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-national-resettlement-scheme-for-conflict-victims/","summary":"The resettlement scheme targeted displaced and conflict-affected communities and framed the effort as rehabilitation and reintegration. This is a durable-institution signal because it creates a programmatic channel for post-conflict recovery rather than ad hoc relief.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"President Tinubu Urges ECOWAS Countries to Ratify, Fully Implement Anti-Corruption Protocol","publisher":"State House","date":"2024-08-19","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-urges-ecowas-countries-to-ratify-fully-implement-anti-corruption-protocol/","summary":"Tinubu publicly backed stronger anti-corruption institutions and regional enforcement norms. This is supportive of durable institutions, but it is still external-facing rhetoric more than proof of domestic enforcement capacity.","question_ids":["6B.9"]},{"title":"Tinubu under fire for appointing son-in-law head of housing agency","publisher":"BusinessDay","date":"2024-02-21","url":"https://businessday.ng/news/article/tinubu-under-fire-for-appointing-son-in-law-head-of-housing-agency/","summary":"The appointment of Tinubu’s son-in-law to the Federal Housing Authority was criticized as nepotism. That is the clearest counterexample to a clean institution-building reading, because it suggests personal/family capture risk inside a housing institution.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"Nigeria charges 76, including minors, with treason after August protests","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"2024-11-01","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nigeria-charges-76-including-minors-with-treason-after-august-protests-3698000","summary":"The state expanded treason charges to 76 defendants, including minors, after the protests. This is negative evidence for durable institutional restraint, because it shows punitive legal capacity being used against dissent rather than neutral, self-limiting institutions.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","3B.4"]},{"title":"Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting","publisher":"Committee to Protect Journalists","date":"2024-10-03","url":"https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/","summary":"Journalists were charged under the Cybercrimes Act despite reform, showing continued legal pressure on scrutiny. That weakens the case that Tinubu built institutions insulated from executive pressure or robust enough to survive him unchanged.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","4B.4"]},{"title":"Nigeria: Police used excessive force to violently quash #Endbadgovernance protests","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-11-28","url":"https://amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/","summary":"Amnesty documented killings, mass detentions, and torture during the crackdown, with authorities denying wrongdoing. This is strong evidence that accountability and restraint institutions were not yet durable in practice.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","4B.4"]},{"title":"Nigeria: 10 Years After Chibok, Schoolchildren Still at Risk","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-04-11","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/11/nigeria-10-years-after-chibok-schoolchildren-still-risk","summary":"HRW said authorities had failed to sustain safe-learning measures, leaving children at continuing risk. This undercuts the claim that Tinubu had built durable child-protection or education-safety institutions in 2024.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8"]}]}
